name: BoardOil Development
description: An interactive preview of a BoardOil development board.

cards.title: Allow linking between stories
cards.description:
## Idea

Link to another story from a card description using a number such as `#123`.

## Questions to explore

- Should a link preview show the story title and column?
- What should happen when the target is archived or unavailable?
- How can the parser leave numbers inside code blocks alone?

**Next step:** agree the link syntax and try it in the Markdown preview.

cards.title: Mermaid diagrams
cards.description:
## Status

Ideation — needs discovery before promotion to implementation.

## Idea

Explore Mermaid diagram support in Markdown content so technical stories and documentation can include diagrams alongside text.

## Discovery questions

- Which editor modes should render diagrams: rich, preview, plain text, or a combination?
- How should invalid Mermaid syntax be presented without disrupting editing?
- What sanitisation and content-security constraints are required?
- Is the client dependency and bundle-size cost justified?
- How should diagrams behave in exported or archived content?

## Promotion gate

Define the intended editing/rendering experience, security boundary, dependency cost, and a small acceptance-testable first slice before moving this beyond Ideation.

cards.title: Story history
cards.description:
## Status

Roadmap idea — discovery required before implementation.

## Objective

Provide an auditable history of meaningful story changes so users can understand what changed, when, and by whom.

## Discovery questions

- Which changes belong in history: content, column, order, tags, assignment, links, and comments?
- What actor, timestamp, and before/after detail should be retained?
- What retention, authorization, and privacy rules apply?
- Should history be exposed through the UI, API, exports, and integrations?
- How should imported or archived stories preserve their history?

## Promotion gate

Define the event model, retention and permission rules, user experience, and a bounded first vertical slice before implementation.

cards.title: Realtime updates for integrations
cards.description:
## Status

Roadmap idea — discovery required before implementation.

## Objective

Allow external integrations to receive timely board and card changes without repeatedly polling the API.

## Discovery questions

- Which delivery mechanism is appropriate: webhooks, server-sent events, MCP subscriptions, or another contract?
- How are subscriptions scoped and authorized per board?
- What ordering, retry, deduplication, and replay guarantees are required?
- Which event payloads are stable public contracts?
- How are delivery failures observed and managed?

## Promotion gate

Choose the integration transport and define its authorization, delivery guarantees, payload contract, observability, and a bounded first vertical slice before implementation.

cards.title: Include pie chart of web traffic
cards.description:
## Goal

The sketch below is an example image for the demo.

cards.title: Bulk card deletion should be idempotent
cards.description:
## Problem

Bulk card deletion fails when a requested card is already absent. Repeating the same request should be safe.

## Example request

```http
POST /api/boards/{boardId}/cards/delete
Content-Type: application/json

{"cardIds": [42]}
```

## Reproduction

1. Delete an existing card with the request above.
2. Send the same card ID again.
3. The second request reports that a card does not exist.

A mixed request containing existing and absent IDs also fails as a whole.

## Expected behavior

Delete the cards that remain and treat missing cards as already deleted. Keep the requested and deleted counts accurate, and preserve board permissions and attachment cleanup.

cards.title: Issue creating new story
cards.description:
## Problem

A new story title can disappear when the session refreshes while the editor is open.

## Reproduction

1. Choose **New story** and type a title.
2. Leave the draft open while the session renews.
3. Return to the editor and check whether the title is still there.

**Expected:** the unsaved draft remains in place until the visitor saves or discards it.

cards.title: Track MCP OAuth refresh-token persistence
cards.description:
## Question

Does an MCP client retain a newly refreshed MCP OAuth token when its connection is idle or restarted?

## Investigation

- Compare the token used before and after a refresh.
- Test an idle connection and a fresh connection separately.
- Confirm whether a client update changes the result.

**Decision:** keep this as compatibility tracking until the client behavior is clear. Do not weaken BoardOil's token rotation to hide a client-side persistence issue.

cards.title: Support Home Assistant OAuth for MCP
cards.description:
## Context

Home Assistant's MCP integration requires a pre-registered confidential OAuth client with a client ID and client secret. BoardOil currently supports dynamically registered public PKCE clients, so this connection needs an additional client type.

## Outcome

Allow a BoardOil system administrator to register and manage confidential OAuth clients so Home Assistant can connect securely to `/mcp/oauth`.

## Acceptance criteria

- System administrators can create a confidential OAuth client with a display name and one or more exact HTTPS redirect URIs.
- BoardOil generates a client ID and client secret, displaying the complete secret only when the client is created.
- Registered confidential clients can use authorization-code and refresh-token flows for `mcp:read` and `mcp:write`.
- OAuth discovery advertises the client-secret authentication method used by Home Assistant.
- PKCE remains required for dynamically registered public clients but is not globally required for confidential clients that do not support it.
- System administrators can list and revoke confidential client registrations.
- Redirect URI validation prevents unsafe or unintended callback destinations.
- Revoking a client invalidates its active authorizations, tokens, and BoardOil OAuth connections.
- Home Assistant can connect to `/mcp/oauth`, complete consent, refresh its token, and call MCP tools.
- Automated coverage exercises discovery, client creation, authorization, token exchange, refresh, revocation, permissions, and redirect validation.
- MCP installation documentation includes Home Assistant setup using the generated client ID and secret.

cards.title: Non docker based install instructions
cards.description:
## Goal

Provide a normal, portable Linux installation using downloadable release archives. The installation must not require Docker, Node.js, the .NET SDK, or a source checkout.

Implementation is deferred; this story remains in Todo.

## Supported release artifacts

Publish framework-dependent archives for mainstream glibc-based Linux distributions:

- `boardoil-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz`
- `boardoil-<version>-linux-arm64.tar.gz`
- SHA-256 checksums for each archive

The host must have the .NET 10 ASP.NET Core Runtime installed. Alpine/musl support is out of scope initially and must be stated explicitly.

Each archive must contain the published API and the compiled Vue frontend under `wwwroot`, so it can run without build tooling.

## Installation layout

Use conventional, separated locations:

- `/opt/boardoil/<version>/` — immutable versioned application files
- `/opt/boardoil/current` — symlink to the active version
- `/etc/boardoil/` — administrator-managed configuration
- `/var/lib/boardoil/` — SQLite database, images, generated signing key, and migration backups

Run BoardOil as a dedicated, unprivileged `boardoil` user. Only the persistent data directory should be writable by that user.

## Portable runtime contract

Document direct foreground execution as the primary, service-manager-neutral method. It must configure:

- `ConnectionStrings__BoardOil=Data Source=/var/lib/boardoil/boardoil.db`
- `BoardOil__ImageRootPath=/var/lib/boardoil/images`
- `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:5000`
- `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED=true`

The executable command is `/opt/boardoil/current/BoardOil.Api`.

Any supervisor may run this contract. Provide systemd as one worked example, while making clear that systemd is optional and OpenRC, runit, s6, and other supervisors can supply the same user, environment, working directory, and command.

## Release pipeline

For a tagged release:

1. Build the Vue frontend with release version metadata.
2. Publish the API for `linux-x64` and `linux-arm64` as framework-dependent deployments.
3. Copy the compiled frontend into each published application's `wwwroot`.
4. Package each target as a versioned `.tar.gz` archive.
5. Smoke-test the extracted x64 archive, including the SPA and `/api/health`.
6. Generate SHA-256 checksums.
7. Attach the archives and checksums to the tagged GitHub release.

## Documentation

Document:

- supported distributions and architectures
- installation of the .NET 10 ASP.NET Core Runtime
- creating the service user and directories with appropriate permissions
- downloading and verifying an archive
- configuration and foreground startup
- optional systemd integration
- reverse proxy, forwarded headers, HTTPS, and secure cookies
- health verification through `/api/health`
- initial administrator setup
- backups, upgrades, rollback, and uninstall
- preserving `/var/lib/boardoil` across upgrades

Upgrade instructions must account for automatic database migrations and their pre-migration backups.

## Out of scope

- Windows or macOS packaging
- an APT, RPM, or other package repository
- Alpine/musl release archives
- dedicated integrations for every Linux init system
- self-contained .NET runtime bundles

cards.title: Job porting 7/7: Add schedule administration and verify the complete port
cards.description:
## Goal

Give administrators a clear way to review and run scheduled jobs.

## Demo checklist

- [x] Show schedules alongside job history.
- [x] Display the configured system timezone.
- [ ] Review the run-now feedback and history link.
- [ ] Verify the complete journey in the browser.

A schedule change should have an understandable result before the administrator leaves the page.

cards.title: Replace Cronos with explicit daily job schedules
cards.description:
## Outcome

Recurring maintenance uses an explicit local time in the configured system timezone.

## Behavior to preserve

- Handle daylight-saving changes without creating duplicate runs.
- Recover a missed occurrence after a restart.
- Keep the daily maintenance time visible as `03:00` in administration.

The schedule definition now describes *when* to run directly, without a cron expression.

cards.title: Job porting 6/7: Add admin job history, details and live updates
cards.description:
## Outcome

Administrators can follow a job from start to completion without manually reloading the page.

- Browse recent jobs and open a detail view.
- Read ordered logs and a clear failure reason.
- Follow live status changes and refresh after reconnecting.

Diagnostic payloads are displayed as text so their contents cannot render as page markup.

cards.title: Job porting 5/7: Activate independent scheduling and execution loops
cards.description:
## Outcome

Scheduling and execution run independently so a long job does not delay the next schedule check.

- Recover incomplete work when the application starts.
- Execute queued jobs one at a time.
- Give cleanup one owner to avoid duplicate runs.

The job history shows each transition as work moves through the queue.

cards.title: Job porting 4/7: Add maintenance handlers and job-history retention
cards.description:
## Outcome

Add the routine maintenance jobs and keep their history for a bounded period.

## Daily work

- Remove expired temporary records.
- Purge old OAuth registrations when appropriate.
- Retain useful job results while clearing older logs.

Maintenance follows the system timezone and reports its result in job history.

cards.title: Job porting 3/7: Port cron schedules and timezone policy
cards.description:
## Outcome

Evaluate recurring schedules using the configured timezone and recover work missed during downtime.

## Cases to handle

- The local clock changes for daylight saving.
- The application restarts after a scheduled time.
- A previous enqueue completed only part of its work.

Each occurrence should have one durable identity so recovery can finish it safely.

cards.title: Job porting 2/7: Port job execution and reliable finalisation
cards.description:
## Outcome

A queued job records its progress and final result so it can survive an application restart.

- Claim one pending job for execution.
- Record logs in order as the handler runs.
- Save success or failure as a terminal state.
- Recover jobs left running by an interrupted process.

Handler changes and job state must be committed consistently.

cards.title: Job porting 1/7: Add EF persistence and migration coverage
cards.description:
## Outcome

Store jobs, their logs, and scheduler state in the database.

## Data model

- `Job` records type, status, and lifecycle timestamps.
- `JobLog` keeps ordered execution messages.
- `SchedulerState` remembers the last evaluated occurrence.

Migration tests cover creating the schema and opening an existing database.

cards.title: Rename OAuth client registration cleanup to purge
cards.description:
## Change

Call the OAuth registration cleanup job **purge** throughout the UI and job definitions.

- Remove scheduler checkpoints for schedule definitions that no longer exist.
- Keep checkpoints for registered schedules, including disabled ones.

The names now describe the action consistently wherever an administrator sees it.

cards.title: Add Once schedules and reusable board resaving
cards.description:
## Outcome

Add one-time schedules and a reusable operation that resaves every board.

## How it runs

1. An administrator requests a run.
2. The scheduler queues one job for each current board.
3. Each job recalculates saved card checklist counts.

Later board-normalization work can reuse the same resave operation.

cards.title: Idea: use markdown checkboxes
cards.description:
## Goal

Show Markdown checklist progress on each board card without opening its description.

- [x] Count checked and unchecked tasks in saved Markdown.
- [x] Show `completed/total` on cards that contain tasks.
- [x] Hide the indicator when a card has no tasks.

The counter follows nested task lists and ignores checkbox examples inside code blocks.

cards.description:
